blocks.value: Overloading is having multiple methods with the same name in the same class, distinguished by different parameter lists: a different number of parameters, different parameter types, or both.

A method's signature is its name plus the number and types of its parameters. Java tells overloaded methods apart by their signature; a class can't define two methods with the exact same one. Constructors can be overloaded the same way, which is exactly what the multiple Pet() constructors from earlier were doing.
